headline: Riyadh airport blast: Biman suspends flights to Saudi capital
summary: Flights are cancelled after a blast at King Khalid International Airport left several injured and disrupted operations.
details: Several people were injured in an attack at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on Saturday afternoon.
Following the blast, the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) temporarily suspended airport operations as a precautionary measure to assess damages and verify security.
Biman Bangladesh Airlines has suspended its Dhaka-Riyadh flights until further notice due to the security situation.
Authorities have not yet confirmed the exact number of casualties or the specific nature of the attack, though they are currently inspecting the airport's infrastructure.
This incident follows a series of attacks on Saudi aviation facilities, including previous strikes by Houthi rebels that killed three Saudi citizens, including a pilot, on Thursday.
Houthi military spokespersons have claimed responsibility for recent attacks, describing them as responses to Saudi aggression in Yemen.
The airport remains one of Saudi Arabia's most critical aviation hubs, and officials stated that further decisions will be made once security checks are completed.
caption:
A blast at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport has left several injured and forced Biman Bangladesh to suspend all flights to the city.

Several people were injured in an attack at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on Saturday afternoon.

Following the blast, the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) temporarily suspended airport operations as a precautionary measure to assess damages and verify security.

Biman Bangladesh Airlines has suspended its Dhaka-Riyadh flights until further notice due to the security situation.

Authorities have not yet confirmed the exact number of casualties or the specific nature of the attack, though they are currently inspecting the airport's infrastructure.

This incident follows a series of attacks on Saudi aviation facilities, including previous strikes by Houthi rebels that killed three Saudi citizens, including a pilot, on Thursday.

Houthi military spokespersons have claimed responsibility for recent attacks, describing them as responses to Saudi aggression in Yemen.

The airport remains one of Saudi Arabia's most critical aviation hubs, and officials stated that further decisions will be made once security checks are completed.

headline_marked: BNP [[activists to stay vigilant at Durga Puja mandaps]] to ensure peace
headline: BNP activists to stay vigilant at Durga Puja mandaps to ensure peace
summary: The party has formed a 12-member Puja observation committee to coordinate volunteer efforts and protect communal harmony during the festival.
details: BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman has called upon party activists to remain vigilant and act as 'sleepless sentinels' at Durga Puja mandaps across the country to prevent security risks.
During a Standing Committee meeting in Gulshan, Dhaka, the party decided to form a 12-member Puja observation committee to oversee the festivities.
Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi stated that BNP activists will work as volunteers in coordination with Puja committees to ensure a peaceful environment.
Rizvi mentioned that while there are 'blueprints of conspiracy' against the country, the party is confident that the Sharad festival will be celebrated in a festive atmosphere.
The meeting also addressed other national issues, including deep concern over the rising prices of essential commodities and the need for better waste management to control dengue.
Additionally, the party leadership urged the government to adopt a zero-tolerance policy against drugs to protect the youth from addiction.
caption:
BNP activists are set to act as volunteers at Durga Puja mandaps to ensure peace and harmony.

BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman has called upon party activists to remain vigilant and act as 'sleepless sentinels' at Durga Puja mandaps across the country to prevent security risks.

During a Standing Committee meeting in Gulshan, Dhaka, the party decided to form a 12-member Puja observation committee to oversee the festivities.

Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi stated that BNP activists will work as volunteers in coordination with Puja committees to ensure a peaceful environment.

Rizvi mentioned that while there are 'blueprints of conspiracy' against the country, the party is confident that the Sharad festival will be celebrated in a festive atmosphere.

The meeting also addressed other national issues, including deep concern over the rising prices of essential commodities and the need for better waste management to control dengue.

Additionally, the party leadership urged the government to adopt a zero-tolerance policy against drugs to protect the youth from addiction.
